subject: Gateway drain & pin safety: preflight and rollback criteria
content:

Subject: Preflight: upcoming maintenance window and version pin question

Hi Karthik,

We are lining up our private deployment maintenance for the week of May 27. Two quick asks before we lock windows:
- We need confirmation on the recommended approach for pinning the Redwood runtime version for our VPC gates so we don’t inadvertently get auto-upgraded during the window.
- We plan to drain the ingress gateway and perform router firmware updates (NetBridge is on copy). Can you confirm: 1) KV cache invalidation approach for short-lived sessions, 2) an acceptable canary cadence for model traffic, and 3) rollback triggers (metrics or error thresholds) you want enforced?

We prefer a narrow overnight window (02:00–05:00 local) but can be flexible if Redwood requires additional time for preflight.

Thanks,
Mina Patel
Infrastructure Ops, Acadia Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, support@netbridge.io

Subject: Re: Preflight: upcoming maintenance window and version pin question

Thanks Mina — good notes. High-level plan below; I’ll own the pin/rollback authorization but want ops on-call on the bridge during the window.

Quick answers:
- Version pinning: we’ll publish a pin manifest for your fleet and gate the control-plane so automatic upgrades are paused for the pinned set. The pin manifest is a small JSON artifact (we'll provide) and can be applied to a subset of nodes for a canary. I recommend pinning the control-plane and model runtime to the last-known-good patch (rwh-2028.05.12).
- KV cache: we will perform a controlled expiry of prefix caches for session tokens that are older than the last 48 hours prior to the cutover; for active sessions we prefer draining rather than hard invalidation.
- Canary cadence: start at 2% of traffic for 30 minutes, measure latency P95 and error-rate, then 10% for 30 minutes, then 25% for 20 minutes before full traffic.
- Rollback triggers: P95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline, 5xx rate > 1.0% absolute increase, token-authorization failures > 0.5% for 15 minutes, or any unrecoverable KV miss causing data corruption (we'll instrument).

Preflight checklist (summary):
- Provide maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf (attached) to bridge attendees.
- NetBridge: confirm router firmware schedule and BGP session drain procedure.
- Ops: snapshot backups and cross-region routing validation done 24h prior.
- Safety: have the rollback-checklist.md ready and a single approval owner for fast revert.

I’m copying Naomi and Soojin to pick up network and runtime-specific steps.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding operational specifics from networking side:

Gateway drain steps (network-facing):
1) Announce maintenance via BGP community to downstream peers 30m prior.
2) Shift VIPs off active gateways by moving weights in F5/Traefik within Control-plane to target standbys.
3) Confirm active sessions < 5/min per instance before eviction; for long polling we’ll drain at session-level.
4) If BGP sessions reset, have prebuilt access to the backup transit (NetBridge to confirm).

Router firmware notes (NetBridge):
- Firmware patching may require rebooting the edge routers; NetBridge to provide the exact time and out-of-band console access.

Runtime precautions (Soojin):
- KV cache: run background reconciliation and a read-through setting that prefers disk if cache misses spike.
- Model shard compatibility: ensure quantized artifacts for the pinned runtime are validated in staging; any model pack incompatibility is a hard abort.

Canary plan: 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% as Karthik suggested. Each step needs a greenlight ping from the on-call and netops.

Attachments: vpc-network-diagram.png (updated to include new transit), rollback-checklist.md

-Naomi

Agree with the plan. A couple of final governance items before I sign the SLA exception:
- Approval owner: Karthik will be the single rollback approver during the window (he signs the revert).
- Rollback cadence: if any one of the rollback triggers trips for > 10 continuous minutes, ops will initiate rollback.
- Postmortem: if rollback occurs, a P0 postmortem draft must be posted within 24 hours and a remediation owner assigned.
- Test run: perform a simulated drain and canary in staging with injected 5xx and KV miss signals 48 hours prior.

I’m authorizing an SLA exception for one additional hour (so NetBridge’s 02:00–04:00 UTC can be extended to 05:00 UTC) provided NetBridge signs off and the staging smoke test passes.
